prompt: Some governments now fund university places only in subjects that lead directly to employment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Nowadays, many governments only give the money for the university courses which can give the students a job after graduation. In my opinion, I agree with this idea partly, because the money of government is limited, but I also think some other subjects are still important.

Firstly, the main reason of studying in university is to find a good job. Many students spend a lot of money for their degree, so they want to get the good salary later. If the government give the fund to subjects like engineering, medicine and computer science, the country will have more doctors and engineers, and this is good for economy. Also the students will not be unemployed after they finish the study. For example, in my country there is many students who are studying the business, but after the graduation they can not find the job in this field.

Secondly, however, we can not say that other subjects are useless. For example history and literature are also important for the society, because they teach us about our culture and our past. If nobody study these subjects, we will lose our identity. Moreover, some students who study art can find the job in media or in advertising, so it is not true that these subjects have no job. Also we should remember that the university is not only the place for the training of the workers.

In conclusion, I agree that the government should give more money to the subjects which are useful for the job market, but I think they should not stop the funding for other subjects completely, because these subjects are also important for the society in the different way.
title: Funding only the degrees that lead to jobs
